references.text: The pillar of cloud is mentioned here for the first time as God's guidance for Israel, the same pillar of cloud that the people see in Exodus 33:10.
The cloud covers the tabernacle and the glory of the Lord fills it, showing God's presence at the entrance of the tent.
The Lord comes down in a pillar of cloud and stands at the entrance of the tent, just as described in Exodus 33:10.
The people have heard that the Lord's cloud is over Israel, confirming the visible presence of the cloud.
The Lord appears in the tent in a pillar of cloud, and the pillar of cloud stands above the entrance of the tent.
The people bow down and worship when they see God's presence, the same act of worship as in Exodus 33:10.
The people bow down and worship the Lord, the same response of worship described in Exodus 33:10.
The cloud fills the house of the Lord so that the priests cannot stand to serve, showing God's glory in the form of a cloud.
God spoke to them in the pillar of cloud, a reference to God communicating through the cloud.
A thematic parallel about the entire congregation gathering before the tent to meet with God's revelation.
